priips.claim: Under PRIIPs, a retail client in the EEA may not be sold a product without a KID. US-domiciled ETFs generally had no KID ready when PRIIPs applied (early 2018). Existing holders can keep or sell but cannot buy more until a compliant KID exists.
priips.note: Article names no brokers. Old (2018); page still online 2026-10-29.

priips.claim: LYNX Broker: 'Retail clients cannot purchase ETFs from countries where the issuer does not publish a KID in accordance with EU regulation.' US ETFs are listed among affected products and cannot be traded unless the client is classified as professional; existing positions can be held or sold. KID obligation from 2018-01-01, extended to UCITS 2023-01-01.

DEGIRO: 'Due to the new PRIIPS legislation, as of the 2nd of January 2018' some foreign products can no longer be bought; 'U.S. products are particularly impacted'; holding or selling remains possible. DEGIRO Czech help page adds that a KID in the local language is required and that DEGIRO generally cannot offer an ETF without it (that Czech page does not mention US ETFs explicitly).
TradeZero Europe: 'TradeZero Europe currently does not offer trading in U.S.-listed ETFs to retail clients' because most US ETF issuers do not provide the KID required for EEA retail clients.
Saxo partner update: US ETFs have no KIDs; white-label partners with the KID solution enabled 'will NOT be able to offer US ETFs to their retail clients anymore'.
priips.date: approx. 2022-09-23 (inferred from URL; not stated on page)

priips.claim: Interactive Brokers: a broker is required to block trading in a PRIIP if no KID is available; US clients are not affected by PRIIPs so issuers of US-listed ETFs do not as a rule create KIDs; European issuers' equivalents have KIDs and are tradable.
priips.note: LOW verification: the page itself returned 403 / redirected (ibkr.info) to the fetch tool; wording taken from search-engine excerpts of the IBKR page.

priips.claim: Trading 212 (staff reply on community forum, as quoted by a search-engine excerpt): US-domiciled ETFs are unavailable due to PRIIPs; most have EU-domiciled PRIIPs/UCITS-compliant equivalents.
priips.note: LOW verification: when I fetched the URL the visible post was by an ordinary user (not staff) saying 'ETFs cannot be traded without a KIID'. No Trading 212 help-centre article found.

priips.claim: XTB: Czech blog Finhacker states XTB 'Neumožňuje obchodování amerických ETFek' (does not allow trading US ETFs; only European equivalents or CFDs). No first-party XTB statement found.

Czech press: Czech retail investors cannot buy VOO/SPY directly through common platforms because of EU PRIIPs legislation (KID not prepared by US managers for the European market); UCITS equivalents such as CSPX are suggested.

Czech brokers differ: Fio banka (Czech bank) is reported to allow clients to trade US ETFs because of a permissive CNB stance (execution only; no advice or active offering); Patria unclear. Fio's own ETF page only says Fio does not offer any ETFs and merely gives access to selected markets, and mentions no PRIIPs/KID.
priips.note: The quote that 'Klienti Fio banky tak i nadale mohou investovat do americkych ETF bez omezeni' comes via a search-engine excerpt of the blog quoting Fio's website; current Fio wording not verified.

priips.claim: CNB Q&A on PRIIPs: a firm that only executes client orders or gives access to a foreign exchange, without actively offering/selling and without advice, is generally not the 'seller' under Art. 13 PRIIPs (so is not itself obliged to deliver the KID). Document does not mention US/third-country funds.

European Parliament written question E-004745/2021 by Eugen Jurzyca (ECR): since 2018 ordinary EU investors cannot invest in US ETFs because they provide no KID; asks the Commission about the regulatory conflict (US issuers say US law bars the performance scenarios the KID requires).
priips.note: Page itself returned empty to the fetch tool; content from a search-engine summary. Commission answer not found. No ESMA/ESA primary text fetched.

cz_tax.claim: Time test: income of an individual from selling securities (shares, ETFs, unit certificates) held more than 3 years is exempt from Czech income tax.
cz_tax.note: Corroborated by finance.cz article of 2025-04-11 ('36 months'): https://www.finance.cz/clanky/552974-jak-se-dani-akcie-kryptomeny-cenne-papiry/. The GFR press release of 2026-01-05 refers to 'splneny cesovy test' but does not state the length. GFR guideline D-59 (search-engine excerpt only, not read) says more than 3 years.

cz_tax.claim: Value test: the exemption for total sale proceeds of securities up to CZK 100,000 per tax period remains in force in 2026 ('hodnotovy test pro osvobozeni stanoveny na 100 tisic korun'). It is measured on proceeds, not profit. Per GFR guidelines (search-engine excerpt of D-59) the time test and value test are alternative conditions and cannot be combined.
cz_tax.note: Proceeds-not-profit and combined-across-brokers wording from ARROWS (https://arws.cz/novinky-v-arrows/efektivni-zdaneni-akcii-a-etf, updated 2026-10-12). Non-combinability of the two tests only via search excerpt of https://financnisprava.gov.cz/assets/cs/prilohy/d-sprava-dani-a-poplatku/Pokyn_GFR-D-59.pdf - not verified.

cz_tax.claim: 40 million CZK cap on exempt income (securities passing the time test): applied only for 2025 (introduced by the 2024 consolidation package), and is ABOLISHED for securities and business shares from 2026-01-01 by Act No. 360/2025 Sb.; it remains for crypto-assets. So there is currently no cap for time-test-exempt securities sales.
cz_tax.publisher: Ministerstvo financi CR (press release); confirmed by GFR 2026-01-05 and dauc.cz 2025-12-11
cz_tax.note: Other sources: https://financnisprava.gov.cz/cs/financni-sprava/media-a-verejnost/tiskove-zpravy-gfr/tiskove-zpravy-2026/danove-novinky-pro-rok-2026 (2026-01-05); https://www.dauc.cz/clanky/16039/prehled-zmen-ve-zdaneni-fo-dle-zakona-c-360-2025-sb (2025-12-11); introduction for 2025: https://www.finance.cz/clanky/552974-jak-se-dani-akcie-kryptomeny-cenne-papiry/ (2025-04-11). Paragraph letters of CZ Income Tax Act sections differ between sources (w, x, u, q) because of amendments - not cited here.

cz_tax.claim: ETFs are taxed like shares on sale; accumulating (Acc) ETFs create no dividend income for the investor, distributing (Dist) ETFs pay dividends taxable in the Czech Republic; tax treatment also depends on fund domicile (often Ireland or Luxembourg).
cz_tax.note: Law-firm marketing article, not an official source. Not verified against the law text.

us_tax.claim: US withholding on dividends paid to a Czech resident: statutory rate 30%, reduced by the US-Czech income tax treaty to 15% (5% for qualifying direct corporate holders). The 15% rate applies to dividends paid by US regulated investment companies (i.e. US ETFs structured as RICs); for REIT dividends only if the individual holds under 10%.
us_tax.publisher: IRS, Tax Treaty Table 1 (Rev. May 2023), Czech Republic row, Article 10(2), footnote w

us_tax.claim: IRS: dividends to nonresident aliens are withheld at 30% or the lesser tax-treaty rate; the beneficial owner claims the treaty article on dividend income by giving Form W-8BEN to the withholding agent.
IRS Form W-8BEN page: foreign beneficial owners give Form W-8BEN to the withholding agent or payer whether or not they claim a reduced rate; current instructions version 10/2021.

US estate tax for nonresident non-citizens: the executor must file Form 706-NA if the date-of-death value of US-situated assets (plus gift tax specific exemption and adjusted taxable gifts) exceeds the filing threshold of USD 60,000; the threshold is not indexed to inflation. IRS lists 'cash and securities' among property that may be includible; the IRS page does not itself spell out that US-listed ETF shares are US-situs (that inference is not sourced here).
us_tax.publisher: IRS, Estate tax for nonresidents not citizens of the United States
us_tax.note: Second IRS page with the same USD 60,000 statement: https://www.irs.gov/node/9899 (updated 2026-06-28).

us_tax.claim: No US estate or gift tax treaty with the Czech Republic: IRS's list of estate and gift tax treaties (Australia, Austria, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, South Africa, Switzerland, UK) does not include the Czech Republic (Czechoslovakia).

dip.claim: DIP (dlouhodoby investicni produkt) can be concluded only from 2024-01-01 ('DIP lze sjednat az od 1. 1. 2024').

Tax deduction: contributions to DIP and other state-supported pension-savings products and long-term-care insurance are deductible together up to CZK 48,000 per year (the limit is shared, not per product). Employer contributions are tax-exempt up to CZK 50,000 per year.
dip.note: GFR 'Danove novinky pro rok 2026' (2026-01-05) does not mention DIP or the 48,000 limit; I found no 2025-2026 change but did not read the law text.

dip.claim: Conditions: no withdrawal before both 10 years (120 months) since the DIP was created and the holder reaching age 60; earlier withdrawal means the claimed tax benefit must be repaid (looking back up to 10 years).
